title: Flask with an app factory for the HTTP API
context: Issue #3 needs an HTTP endpoint; nothing in the repo chose a framework yet, but Flask 3.1 was already installed.
options: FastAPI: async and auto-generated OpenAPI docs, adds pydantic and uvicorn
Flask: synchronous like the sqlite3 layer, already installed, one dependency
Stdlib http.server: no dependency, but routing and error handling by hand
choice: Flask, create_app() factory, one SQLite connection per request
why: The storage layer is synchronous, so async gains nothing. The factory takes a DatabaseConfig so tests use a temp database; per-request connections are closed in teardown.

title: Consistent JSON envelope: {data: ...} on success, {error: {code, message}} on failure
context: Acceptance criteria require a consistent response format and meaningful errors.
options: Return the bare link object and Flask's default HTML errors
Envelope with a stable machine-readable error code plus a human message, applied to framework errors (404/405) too
why: Clients can branch on error.code (invalid_url, unsupported_scheme, alias_taken, ...) without parsing messages. Status codes: 201 created, 400 bad input, 409 alias taken, 503 if no code could be allocated.

anchors.snippet: def error_response(status: int, code: str, message: str):

title: URL validation is syntactic: http(s) scheme, a host, no whitespace/control chars, max 2048 chars
context: Issue asks to validate URLs and allow only HTTP and HTTPS.
options: Also resolve DNS or check reachability: catches typos but slow and flaky
Also block private/localhost hosts or check malware lists
why: The shortener never fetches the destination, so there is no SSRF risk; reachability checks would slow every request. The scheme allowlist is what blocks javascript:, data: and file: links. Abuse screening (phishing, malware) is deliberately left out; flagging it in case you want it.

title: Accept optional alias and expires_at in POST /api/links
context: Issue #3 only names the destination URL, but #2 added aliases and #4 must reject expired links.
options: URL only, as the issue states; aliases and expiry unreachable from the API
Optional alias (validated by #2's path) and expires_at (ISO 8601 with a required timezone)
why: Without them the alias path from #2 and the expiry handling #4 depends on cannot be used. This goes slightly beyond the issue's literal scope; easy to drop if you would rather keep it minimal.

title: Build short_url from SHORTY_BASE_URL, falling back to the request host
context: The endpoint must return the complete shortened URL.
options: Always use request.host_url: zero config, but wrong behind proxies and spoofable through the Host header
Require a configured base URL: correct, but breaks local dev without config
Configured SHORTY_BASE_URL, falling back to the request host when unset
why: Production should set the public domain; local runs work without setup. Worth setting in any deployment because the fallback trusts the Host header.
